tasks.title: Money as integers
tasks.statement: Amounts were stored as fractional numbers. Output the total in cents — an integer: column `cents` = the sum of amount·100, rounded to an integer with ROUND and cast to an integer type (CAST … AS INTEGER). Sum the values rounded per row; do not round the total.
tasks.hint: Round every row: CAST(ROUND(amount * 100) AS INTEGER), then SUM.

tasks.title: Closure of an attribute set
tasks.statement: Functional dependencies are a list of pairs [left side, right side] (each is a list of attributes). Write attr_closure(attrs, fds): a sorted list of all attributes functionally determined by the set attrs (including attrs itself). Example: fds = [[["a"],["b"]],[["b"],["c"]]], attrs = ["a"] → ["a","b","c"].
tasks.hint: Repeat: if the left side of a dependency is already in the result, add the right side; until nothing is added.

tasks.title: Candidate keys
tasks.statement: Given the attributes relation and the functional dependencies fds (as in the previous task). Write candidate_keys(relation, fds): the list of all candidate keys (minimal under inclusion) — each key is a sorted list, and the list of keys is sorted. A key is a set whose closure equals all attributes.
tasks.hint: Go through the sets in increasing size; skip supersets of keys already found.

tasks.title: Third normal form
tasks.statement: A relation is a set of attributes; you are given a set of dependencies (one attribute on the right) and the set of prime attributes (those that belong to some candidate key) prime. Write is_3nf(fds, prime, keys): True if for every dependency X → A either A is in X, or X is a superkey (contains some key from keys), or A is a prime attribute (in prime).
tasks.hint: For each dependency check the three permitting conditions; if none holds, it is not 3NF.

tasks.title: Lossless decomposition
tasks.statement: A relation with attributes relation was decomposed into two parts r1 and r2 (sets of attributes that together cover relation). The FDs fds are known. Write lossless_binary(relation, fds, r1, r2): True if the shared attributes r1 ∩ r2 functionally determine all of r1 or all of r2 (the closure of the shared attributes contains r1 or r2).
tasks.hint: The closure of the shared attributes must cover one of the parts.

tasks.title: Decomposing a flat table
tasks.statement: A flat table is a list of rows [order, client, city, product, price]. Write split_table(rows): a triple of lists [orders [order, client, product], clients [client, city], products [product, price]] — clients and products without repeats, sorted; orders in the original order. If a client or a product occurs with different city or price values, keep the first one.
tasks.hint: Dictionaries with setdefault for clients and products; orders in row order.

tasks.title: Ordered identifiers
tasks.statement: An identifier is a pair [time in milliseconds, counter within the millisecond]. Write ordered_ids(times): for a list of insertion moments (non-strictly increasing) return the identifiers: the counter equals the number of earlier insertions in the same millisecond. The result must then be strictly increasing as pairs.
tasks.hint: Reset the counter when the millisecond changes.

tasks.title: Tenant isolation
tasks.statement: Rows are lists [tenant, id, value]. The primary key is the pair (tenant, id). Write scope_by_tenant(rows, tenant): a dictionary "id → value" only for the rows of this tenant; if a pair occurs several times, the last row wins. The dictionary keys are the id as a string.
tasks.hint: A dictionary over only the rows of the needed tenant; the last entry overwrites the previous one.
